chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 441 – The Memorial: Li Huowang’s Desperate Gambit for Zhuge Yuan
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang makes a heart-wrenching choice as Zhuge Yuan dies. Can a final, brutal act force his friend back as a hallucination?
og_title: Chapter 441 – The Memorial: When Grief Becomes a Cosmic Loophole
og_description: The price of love in the Dao-Twisted World: Li Huowang beheads his dying friend to force a resurrection through his own cursed power.
twitter_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 441 – Bereavement
twitter_description: The Heart-Element’s ultimate test: a death, a choice, and the birth of a new hallucination.

lore_anchors.definition: A forbidden alchemical ritual that overwrites the body’s natural Five Phases cycle with a parasitic, unnatural one, consuming the practitioner’s own substance as fuel.
A rare human constitution whose owner can transform belief into reality; hallucinations around a Heart-Element can become tangible, living beings.
A Heart-Element member of the Zuowandao with the ability to swap bodies with others at will.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Li Huowang behead Zhuge Yuan?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He hoped that by killing him personally, Zhuge Yuan would become one of the “lingering hallucinations” bound to a Heart-Element, and later be made real again through cultivation.
Yes, but only after Li Huowang was back in his own Heart-Element body. Zhuge Yuan did not appear immediately; the transfer required the right medium.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the Intercalating the Five Phases?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is a sacrificial ritual that uses the caster’s own body and lifespan as fuel, overwriting their Five Phases with a parasitic, unnatural “intercalated” phase that keeps them alive at a terrible cost.
